record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure and table content is garbled in the extracted text, but the main reported results and Table 2 are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures single-neuron selectivity for grammatical and conceptual contrasts and concludes that strongly selective grammatical neurons are rare. This is a refinement/challenge to neuron-level job claims, though it does not reproduce the original audit or measure the same job categories.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-level selectivity across minimal-pair paradigms, models, and thresholds. It also reports probe/behavior comparisons and ablations; those do not measure the claimed shares of named neuron jobs or explanation accuracy on held-out activations. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It measures how strongly single last-token residual-stream coordinates separate grammatical from ungrammatical minimal pairs (NSI) on BLiMP/COMPS. It does not test whether neurons (MLP units or neuron poles) have one main job, two related jobs, or no understood job. A coordinate insensitive to grammaticality may still have a clear job of another kind. Low tuning breadth over 68 tested contrasts is not a job-share audit. This is a related but different construct. The only link to the claim is citing Bills et al. (an original source) on polysemanticity.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that single-unit grammatical selectivity is sparse, weak and narrowly tuned, and that strongly selective 'grandmother neurons' are rare. They also find that whole-vector decodability, single-unit NSI and behaviour are dissociated, and that targeted group ablations do not reveal a behaviourally privileged high-NSI set. Note that their 'neurons' are last-token residual-stream dimensions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a probe-free, permutation-normalized minimal-pair selectivity index and activation measurements across linguistic paradigms, rather than auditing neuron-pole explanations or testing their descriptions on held-out activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to NSI threshold, similarity metric (Pearson versus Spearman and cosine), sentence pairing, and critical-token deletion. It reports that random same-label pairs have raw separability near 0.50 but no NSI > 2 units; cross-item good–bad pairing creates sporadic high-NSI artifacts. Critical-token deletion in the clean one-prefix subset reduces mean raw separability from 0.0753 to 0.0011; deleting a matched non-critical token leaves it at 0.0746.

fits_no_version.finding: Across seven decoder checkpoints (0.4B–8B), only about 2.5–3.9% of last-token residual coordinates have NSI>0 for an average BLiMP/COMPS paradigm. Mean breadth is 1.7–2.7 of 68 paradigms. Only 2–6 paradigms per model contain any NSI>2 unit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single residual-stream coordinates in LLMs rarely show strong, selective sensitivity to grammatical minimal-pair contrasts; such selectivity is sparse, weak and narrow.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen3-0.6B, zeroing groups that contain the three NSI>2 coordinates is no more damaging than same-size random groups (all p_rand ≥ 0.109; Table 1/9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High activation selectivity of a residual coordinate for a grammatical contrast does not indicate privileged causal reliance.

record.problems: The study uses English, templated BLiMP/COMPS minimal pairs and last-token residual-stream dimensions, and its authors caution that results may differ for other data, positions, components, or neuron definitions. NSI measures item-wise response-profile selectivity, not whether a neuron has a single interpretable job. The cross-model survey covers seven decoder-only checkpoints only, up to 8B. Empirical-null calibration is limited: no unit survives the reported Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and the authors describe NSI > 2 as an operational threshold rather than a Gaussian significance cutoff. The ablation follow-up is confined to three paradigms in one checkpoint and reuses the same 1,000 pairs for selection and evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include raw-separability layer-localization results, the reported probe/behaviour correlations, pairing/deletion-control table values, alternative-metric threshold values, or targeted-ablation outcomes: these do not directly measure the named-job shares in V2. The paper's ablation findings are discussed in gate_note and authors_conclusion.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B, no neuron-pole audit, no job-share categories.
No per-neuron job audit in any model. Units are residual-stream coordinates, not MLP neurons. No MoE models, nothing above 8B.
No vision models or canonical polysemantic neuron re-analysis.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No explanations tested against where neurons fire.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 link and limits_scope label are dropped. NSI measures item-wise sensitivity to chosen grammatical contrasts in residual coordinates, not whether a neuron has one interpretable job. The essay's job-share claim is about MLP neuron poles, so these numbers neither support nor challenge it. Grammatical rarity of selective units is compatible with neurons having clear non-grammatical jobs.

versions.untested_parts: Does not study Qwen3-32B or audit positive/negative neuron poles, named jobs, or the stated 90%/7%/2–4% shares.
Tests neuron selectivity on linguistic minimal-pair contrasts in seven checkpoints, not the stated job-share categories; no mixture-of-experts models or models above 8B are studied.
Does not study InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not compare vision architectures, regularization, or interpretability tools, or estimate interpretable-neuron shares for InceptionV1-sized models.
Does not test whether attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons explain its behaviour without a replacement model.
Does not test natural-language explanations against held-out activating examples or measure where a neuron fires after an explanation is written.
Does not score automated neuron explanations by simulating their activations on new text.
